title: Random-sign moment comparison
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $X,r:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, let $q\in[1,\infty]$, and let $a\in\mathbb R$. Suppose $X$ belongs to $L^q(\mu)$, has integral zero, and is independent of $r$, where $r$ is a measurable Rademacher variable: it equals $1$ or $-1$ almost everywhere and each value has probability $1/2$. Then $\|a+X/2\|_{L^q(\mu)}\le\|a+rX\|_{L^q(\mu)}$, where these are the extended $L^q$ norms.
hypotheses_covered: $r$ is a measurable Rademacher variable with equally likely signs
replaced: Let $X$ be a centered real random variable on a probability space, let $1\le q\le\infty$, and assume $X\in L^q$. If $r$ is an independent measurable uniform sign in $\{-1,1\}$, then for every $a\in\bbr$, $\|a+X/2\|_q\le\|a+rX\|_q$, including the essential-supremum norm.
